newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 16.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- FKI MAKES BID APPROACH FOR NEWMAN TONKS GROUP

The Halifax-based engineering group FKI has made a 150 million stg bid approach to Newman Tonks, maker of architectural hardware with a stock market value of 130 million stg. The move follows a 136 million stg rights issue last year which led to a spate of acquisitions by FKI. Jeff Whalley, FKI chairman, has said his ambition is to take the group into the FT-SE 100 index.
-- REPORT TO PRESS FOR TIGHTER LME RULES

The Securities and Investment Board report into the London metals market is expected to back the tightening up of the London Metal Exchange's rule-book, while leaving unique market characteristics unchanged. Raj Bagri, Metal Exchange chairman, said he wanted to tighten up regulation as long ago as last June, before the Sumitomo scandal. The LME has also unveiled plans to introduce rules allowing it to seek more information on large positions of both members and their clients.
-- HEATHROW SLOTS ON KEY ROUTES THE PRICE FOR BA-AMERICAN

British Airways and American Airlines have been told to give priority to surrendering take-off and landing slots at Heathrow to four key transatlantic routes as a condition of clearing their alliance. Two of the routes, London to Dallas Fort Worth and London to Boston, were singled out by the Department of Trade and the Office of Fair Trading for top priority because of the two airlines have a majority share of services. The government feels it could take ten years to be sure that the restrictions imposed on the alliance will result in more competition.
THE TIMES
-- MCDONNELL DOUGLAS AND BOEING IN 13 BILLION STG MERGER

The world's biggest aerospace company is to be created with a 13.3 billion stg merger of Boeing and the US aircraft manufacturer McDonnell Douglas. This poses a major challenge to the European consortium Airbus Industrie. The deal will create a company with 200,000 employees, sales of about 50 billion dollars a year, with more than a 50 per cent share of the world's commercial airline market and a combined order book of more than 100 billion dollars.
-- BUSINESS WANTS ANTI-INVESTMENT TAX BIAS TO END

Business leaders are attempting to remove what they see as a clear fiscal bias against investment, which is holding back the UK's economic competitiveness, by proposing radical reforms to Britain's corporate tax system. The proposal is one of a range of yet-unpublished recommendations business leaders will make after a 21-month study of the role of business and public policy. The report of the Commission on Public Policy and British Business is to be published next month.
-- BRITAIN GETTING IT RIGHT, SAYS OECD

According to the latest economic outlook from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, Britain is set to enjoy a virtuous combination of healthy growth and falling unemployment, coupled with low inflation. The only bad point for the British economy is the state of the public finances. The OECD notes that fiscal consolidation has been proceeding relatively slowly and that significant further progress will have to be made if the Government's aim of a balanced budget in the medium term is to be achieved.
THE GUARDIAN
-- LLOYD'S TAKES NAMES TO COURT

Lloyd's of London will launch a courtroom offensive in an effort to force reluctant Names to pay more than 200 million stg. The Names have refused to sign Lloyd's recent 3.2 billion stg rescue package. The deal was accepted by most of the market's 34,000 Names but a hardline group of Names has pledged to continue to fight Lloyd's. Lloyd's is bringing cases against Geoffrey Lyons, Dennis Leighs and David Wilkinson.
-- ALLIANCE AND LEICESTER PLANS TO GROW

Alliance and Leicester plans to expand further into banking, insurance and unit trusts after its 2.9 billion stg stock market floatation in the spring. The company will still be small by the standards of other banks and could prove to be vulnerable to a predator. To avoid a takeover it plans to "rapidly put on weight". A spokesman denied reports that Alliance planned a rights issue to raise extra cash from those savers and borrowers who are being offered shares worth about 1,000 stg each.
-- ANOTHER 150,000 PEOPLE FACE NEW YEAR WITH NO JOB TO GO TO
According to a Labour Party study, more than 150,000 jobs are to be lost in the new year, despite signs that the official unemployment claimant total is about to drop below two million.

The figures, which were put together by employment spokesman Peter Hain from company and government announcements, show that job cuts are planned from banking and construction to textiles and public services.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- HOLLYWOOD STUDIOS REFUSE BSKYB PAY-PER-VIEW RIGHTS
Hollywood studios Disney and MCA have refused to sign exclusive pay-per-view movie deals with Rupert Murdoch's BSkyB.

The move will threaten BSkyB's efforts to dominate the PPV market in the UK in the age of digital television. The studios, with the exception of Murdoch's Fox, are intent on supplying their movies on a pay-as-you-watch basis to any distribution platform, such as satellite, cable or digital terrestrial.
-- SFA FACES CHALLENGE OVER RESPONSIBILITY

City regulator, the Securities and Futures Authority, is coming under pressure to drop its proposals to make top banking executives responsible for failures of their financial firms after the discovery that the rules breach European law. The regulations would shift the burden of proof in disciplinary cases so that senior executives would have to prove they acted properly rather than the SFA having to show that they failed in their duties.
-- INDUSTRY PAY DEALS STAY LOW

According to the CBI's latest pay databank, pay settlements in manufacturing are continuing to decline, proving fresh evidence that wage inflation is at least under control despite rising prices in the high street and housing market. Settlements in manufacturing averaged 2.9 per cent for the three months to the end of October, below the headline rate for inflation. The figures will be welcomed by Chancellor Kenneth Clarke as he seeks to fend off pressures for a further increase in interest rates to avoid rising inflation in the run-up to the election.
